text: By the time the first tenants moved into Garrow Heights in late autumn 2019, the financing had already become part of local lore. Council filings now confirm that the £48 million housing scheme was underwritten by Calloway Mutual, the midsized lender whose regional property desk has quietly backed a string of civic developments across Northfold in recent years. The bank approved the final facility in March 2018, following a six-month review of plans drawn up by Merren & Vale Housing Partnership. Former project director Alistair Wren said Calloway’s loan terms “kept the scheme alive” after a promised public grant was delayed. Built on the site of the old Garrow goods yard, the estate now holds 312 flats and maisonettes.
